name: persuasion_strategy
instructions:
Classify the persuader message according to the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it uses in a charity-donation conversation.

Key distinctions:
- Acknowledgement: Reacting to what the persuadee said (agreeing with their opinion/fact/concern)
- Praise-user: Bare affirmation ("Great!", "Awesome!") right after persuadee commits to donating
- Thank: Expressions of gratitude
- Greeting: Hello, Hi, or responses to "how are you"
- Ask-donation-amount: Questions asking persuadee to name their own donation amount
- Proposition-of-donation: Asking whether they will donate at all (yes/no choice)
- Emotion-appeal: Statistics/facts about child suffering, sadness expressions, "imagine..." statements
- Logical-appeal: Claims donation has impact, moral reasoning, cost comparisons
- Credibility-appeal: Facts about the charity's history/reach/accomplishments, website links
- Donation-information: Mechanics only - payment range ($0-$2), deduction from task payment, how to pay
- Foot-in-the-door: Persuading by emphasizing even small donations matter ("even 5 cents", "pocket change")
- Personal-related-inquiry: Questions about persuadee's own life/experience/past donations
- Personal-story: Persuader sharing a personal anecdote (rare)
- Self-modeling: Persuader describing their own giving or matching offers
- Source-related-inquiry: Questions about whether persuadee knows Save the Children
- Task-related-inquiry: Other general questions about opinions/preferences
- Off-task: Irrelevant tangents (rare)
- Other: Fillers/filler responses, hostility, meta-task remarks, arguments

criteria.acknowledgement: Agreeing with or validating something the persuadee said
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Asking persuadee to specify how much they want to donate
criteria.credibility-appeal: Facts about the charity's history, reach, accomplishments, or website
criteria.donation-information: Mechanics of donating - payment range, task payment deduction, payment methods
criteria.emotion-appeal: Statistics about child suffering, sadness expressions, or 'imagine' statements
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Emphasizing that even small donations matter significantly
criteria.greeting: Greeting or response to 'how are you'
criteria.logical-appeal: Claims that donation has impact, moral reasoning, or cost-benefit comparisons
criteria.other: Fillers, hostility, meta-task remarks, or arguments
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Questions about persuadee's life, experience, or past donations
criteria.personal-story: Persuader sharing their own personal anecdote
criteria.praise-user: Affirmation after persuadee commits to donating
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Asking whether they will donate at all
criteria.self-modeling: Persuader describing their own giving or matching donations
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Questions about whether persuadee knows Save the Children
criteria.task-related-inquiry: General questions about opinions, preferences, or other topics
